posts.source: 虚弱的实践和火热的研究.md
posts.description: Qinlizhe research is arriving remarkably smoothly. What happens when participation comes before a struggle over power?
posts.context: Qinlizhe (亲历者) is a locally developed name for people speaking from first-hand experience and witnessing. This essay questions its institutional use rather than treating it as a direct equivalent of survivor or service user.

posts.source: 从一个提问开始：Mad Studies 如何面对非英语世界？.md
posts.description: I asked about the non-English-speaking world. Why did the answer return to differences within the English-speaking one?

posts.source: 舍不得离开疯板凳的人.md
posts.description: My contact with psychiatry was brief. My attachment to this mad position is not. Why am I still here?
posts.context: Qinlizhe (亲历者), retained here in pinyin, carries first-hand experience and witnessing. It does not settle the questions of identity this essay is asking.

posts.source: 精神健康公益合作中的幻象与结构不对称.md
posts.author: Qinlizhe Mad Studies Collective
posts.description: Who gets to declare a beginning, define a community, and ask for solidarity? A response from within Chinese mental-health gongyi.
posts.context: Gongyi (公益) is retained for a heterogeneous field of public-interest work, including mutual support, advocacy, education, and organized projects. The quoted passages below are translated from Chinese. Linked article titles are descriptive translations, not verified official English titles.

posts.source: 什么时候可以说自己想说的话？.md
posts.description: Shared commitments can create relationships we feel forced to maintain. Where does that leave anger, dislike, and the wish to speak honestly?

posts.source: 不用做端水大师的时刻.md
posts.description: For once, we could speak without immediately adding that there are good psychiatrists too. Then I caught myself doing it again.

posts.source: 在幸存者研究和疯狂研究的现场.md
posts.description: I went looking for people who might already have solved our problems. I found living arguments, labour boundaries, and no finished answers.

posts.source: 我们还没有答案的问题.md
posts.description: Questions about representation, labour, harm, collaboration, refusal, and what it takes to act together without pretending to be one.
posts.context: Qinlizhe (亲历者) is retained rather than substituted with survivor, patient, or service user. The questions leave room for different positions and relationships to psychiatry.

posts.source: Mad Studies 的挑战和局限.md
posts.description: Reading with Beresford and Rose while asking who gets to enter Mad Studies, speak for it, and make knowledge count.

posts.source: 用zine重新思考精神医学：一次课堂实践.md
posts.description: A short account of using eight-page zines to think about mental health, knowledge, care, and power.
